nodes.title: Nagurney projected-system well-posedness theorem
nodes.description: Nagurney projected-system theorem gives global solutions and continuous dependence under one-sided Lipschitz and linear-growth conditions.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named external theorem directly used in the global-flow proof.

nodes.title: Global well-posedness under global Lipschitzness
nodes.description: A globally Lipschitz vector field on X admits a unique continuous global projected flow.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable formal lemma for global projected dynamics.

nodes.title: McShane extension theorem
nodes.description: Coordinatewise McShane extension extends the locally Lipschitz restriction on K_R to a globally Lipschitz map.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named external theorem directly used in localization.

nodes.title: Lipschitz extensions on bounded regions
nodes.description: For locally Lipschitz Q, each bounded region has a globally Lipschitz extension agreeing with Q and a continuous global projected flow.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable localization lemma.

nodes.title: Localization exit times
nodes.description: Fixes localized flows and defines the first exit time sigma_{K_R}(x) from the localization ball.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable definition used in compatibility, patching, and regularity arguments.

nodes.title: Agreement before exit
nodes.description: Before the smaller localization exits, it solves the original projected dynamics and agrees with larger localizations.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Compatibility lemma directly used to patch flows.

nodes.title: Constructing the maximal local flow
nodes.description: The supremum of localized exit times defines a positive-lifetime local flow solving the original projected dynamics.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Central local-flow construction.

nodes.title: Maximality and uniqueness
nodes.description: The patched lifetime is maximal and every local solution agrees with the unique maximal local solution map.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable uniqueness and maximality result.

nodes.title: Regularity of tau and G
nodes.description: The maximal lifetime is lower semicontinuous and the local flow is continuous on its domain.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Direct prerequisite for measurability.

nodes.title: Local Lipschitzness implies well-behaved projected dynamics
nodes.description: If X is closed and convex and Q is locally Lipschitz, the projected dynamics are well behaved; under global Lipschitzness the maximal flow is global.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof and directly invokes preceding lemmas.

nodes.title: Dynamic solvers are measurable
nodes.description: Every dynamic solver g_Q is measurable from X to X disjoint union {dagger}.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies the full proof.

nodes.title: Terminal-behavior decomposition
nodes.description: The cases C1 finite lifetime, C2 infinite nonconvergence, and C3 infinite convergence determine dagger versus trajectory limit.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Indispensable decomposition in the measurability proof.

nodes.title: Infinite-survival set
nodes.description: A_infty is the countable intersection of open survival sets A_n and is Borel.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named measurable set reused in later measurability construction.

nodes.title: Measurable asymptotic limsup and liminf
nodes.description: Rational-time coordinate limsup and liminf maps are measurable on A_infty and equal the real-time asymptotic limsup and liminf.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable coordinate construction for convergence and measurability.

nodes.title: Convergence set and limit map
nodes.description: The convergence set Xi is Borel; on Xi the coordinate limits define a Borel limit map L into X.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Indispensable construction for the measurable solver.

nodes.title: Measurable solver pieces
nodes.description: The condition sets C1, C2, C3 are Borel and give measurable preimages for g_Q.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Final measurable-piece argument used to prove the solver's measurability.

nodes.title: Dominated convergence / Cesaro averaging
nodes.description: Dominated convergence, equivalently Cesaro averaging, identifies the long-run time average with the limit value.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named proof tool directly used in root containment.

nodes.title: Terminal outcomes lie among projected roots
nodes.description: Every ordinary dynamic-solver outcome is a root of the projected vector field, while nonconvergent outcomes are dagger.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Formal root-containment lemma reused by the prevalence conclusion.

nodes.title: Finite reachable outcomes exactly when projected roots are finite
nodes.description: A dynamic solver has finitely many reachable terminal outcomes exactly when its projected vector field has finitely many roots.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies the nontrivial root-containment argument used by this body proposition.

nodes.title: Submersion probes imply prevalent finiteness of reachable terminal outcomes
nodes.description: Under convexity, root compactness, and submersion-probe hypotheses, prevalent dynamics have finitely many reachable terminal outcomes.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Root compactness
nodes.description: The projected-root set lies in a common compact set, and the state space has the required C2 boundary regularity.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Directly invoked in prevalence finiteness and boundary closedness arguments.

nodes.title: Closed convex state space
nodes.description: The state space X is closed and convex.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Direct hypothesis of the finite-root corollary.

nodes.title: Interior and boundary projection formula
nodes.description: For C2 boundary, QTC equals Q in the interior and QTCP on the boundary, with QTCP using the positive normal component.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Graph-relevant decomposition used by the boundary-root arguments.

nodes.title: Closed discrete sets in compact sets are finite
nodes.description: A subset closed and discrete in a topological space is finite when contained in a compact set.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Compactness lemma used to prove finite roots.

nodes.title: Projected roots split into interior and boundary roots
nodes.description: Projected-field roots are contained in roots of Q or QTCP, and those two root sets are closed in their domains.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Decomposition and closedness result used by the finite-root corollary.

nodes.title: Boundary-root encoding
nodes.description: The boundary roots are encoded by the C1 map tilde Q(x,alpha)=Q(x)-alpha n(x).
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable smooth encoding for boundary transversality.

nodes.title: Boundary transversality implies discrete roots
nodes.description: If tilde Q is transverse to zero, then the boundary projected-root set is discrete in the boundary.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Boundary discreteness lemma used by the prevalence theorem.

nodes.title: Parametric transversality from a submersion
nodes.description: For a C^r submersion F on parameter-manifold product, almost every parameter fiber is transverse to zero.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Central parametric transversality theorem used for prevalence.

nodes.title: Regularity required for parametric transversality
nodes.description: When dim Z equals n, C1 regularity suffices; higher regularity is required when dim Z exceeds n for Sard projection.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Source-visible qualification of the parametric theorem.

nodes.title: Guillemin–Pollack transversality reference
nodes.description: Guillemin and Pollack is cited for the Sard regularity requirement.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Citation directly supports the regularity remark.

nodes.title: Preimage theorem
nodes.description: The preimage theorem makes the zero set of the submersion a submanifold with tangent kernel.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named theorem directly used in the parametric-submersion proof.

nodes.title: Sard's theorem
nodes.description: Sard theorem makes critical values of the projection measure zero.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named theorem directly used in the parametric-submersion proof.

nodes.title: Rank–nullity theorem
nodes.description: Rank-nullity relates projection rank and fiber-map rank in the parametric-submersion proof.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named theorem directly used in the parametric-submersion proof.

nodes.title: Transversality gives discrete zero sets
nodes.description: When n equals dim Z, transversality to zero makes the zero set zero-dimensional and hence discrete.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Graph-relevant bridge from transversality to discreteness.

nodes.title: Perturbed evaluation maps
nodes.description: The finite-dimensional probe evaluation maps e^Q and e^tildeQ are defined.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Formal maps to which parametric submersion is applied.

nodes.title: Prevalence via a submersion probe
nodes.description: If the perturbed evaluation maps are C1 submersions, prevalent dynamics have discrete interior and boundary root sets.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Central prevalence theorem.

nodes.title: Prevalent finiteness of projected roots
nodes.description: Under convexity, compactness, and submersion-probe hypotheses, prevalent Q have finitely many roots of QTC.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Finite-root conclusion used to bound reachable terminal outcomes.

nodes.title: Basin-Size Concentration
nodes.description: The subsection fixes A_epsilon={s_x* <= 1-epsilon} for posterior concentration of basin size.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable notation setup for the Bayesian bounds.

nodes.title: Bayes denominator bound
nodes.description: Posterior probability of A_epsilon is bounded by likelihood-ratio and prior numerator and denominator factors.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Formal bound reused by posterior-concentration proofs.

nodes.title: Support near one
nodes.description: If 1 is in support of Pi, every epsilon admits eta<epsilon with Pi(A_eta)<1.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Support lemma used to choose the denominator parameter.

nodes.title: Support near one implies exponential posterior concentration
nodes.description: Support of the basin-size prior near one yields exponential decay of the posterior probability of A_epsilon.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Dropping eta under a polynomial prior-density lower bound
nodes.description: A polynomial prior-density lower bound near one yields an explicit polynomial-times-exponential posterior bound for A_epsilon.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Polynomial prior-density lower bound near one
nodes.description: The basin-size prior density is bounded below by a polynomial rate near one.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Directly invoked in the posterior-size proof.

nodes.title: Beta-prior posterior concentration
nodes.description: A Beta(alpha,beta) prior updates to Beta(alpha+n,beta), yielding an exponential posterior tail bound with a polynomial prefactor.
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Gautschi's inequality
nodes.description: Gautschi inequality bounds the relevant Gamma ratio polynomially.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Cited external inequality directly used in the beta-prior proof.

nodes.title: Spike-and-Slab Prior
nodes.description: Defines the spike-and-slab prior, q_n, and the posterior spike-mass formula.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable setup used by the spike-rate proof.

nodes.title: Moment bound from near--1 tail
nodes.description: E_W[S^n] is bounded by a near-one tail integral plus (1-delta)^n.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Moment estimate reused by the polynomial-tail corollary.

nodes.title: Polynomial tail implies polynomial moment decay
nodes.description: A polynomial upper bound on the near-one tail implies E_W[S^n] <= C n^{-gamma} eventually.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Moment-rate result reused by the spike-and-slab proposition.

nodes.title: Spike-and-slab posterior rate
nodes.description: If the slab's near-one tail is O(u^gamma), posterior mass outside the spike is O(n^{-gamma}).
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Two-sided bounds for L_k(n) (fixed x*)
nodes.description: The MFM likelihood L_k(n) has explicit two-sided power bounds with exponent delta_k.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Likelihood-rate lemma reused by the MFM theorem.

nodes.title: Dirichlet moment formula
nodes.description: The Dirichlet moment formula gives E[s_1^n] as a Gamma ratio.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Named formula directly used in MFM likelihood proofs.

nodes.title: Monotonicity of L_k(n)
nodes.description: For fixed alpha and n, L_k(n) decreases with k.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Monotonicity lemma used by the MFM theorem.

nodes.title: Rate-tight concentration of P(K=1 | H_n(x*))
nodes.description: Under the fixed-x* MFM assumptions, posterior mass outside K=1 is Theta(n^{-alpha/2}).
nodes.inclusion_reason: The appendix supplies its proof.

nodes.title: Mixed-logit equilibrium price bounds
nodes.description: Skerlos et al. supply lower and upper bounds for mixed-logit equilibrium prices.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Cited external result directly used in the smooth-domain construction.

nodes.title: A smooth compact price domain
nodes.description: The l^{2p}-type set X_p contains the price box, is compact and convex, has smooth boundary, and lies in the positive orthant for large p.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable construction for the application domain.

nodes.title: A transported Banach structure
nodes.description: Transported operations and norm make the parametrized dynamics class a Banach space via a finite-dimensional linear isometry.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Reusable construction for the application dynamics class.

nodes.title: Injective dynamics parametrization
nodes.description: The parameter-to-dynamics map is injective, so transported operations and the transported norm are well defined.
nodes.inclusion_reason: Explicit local assumption directly required by the Banach-space construction.

ambiguities.question: Should proof blocks for body propositions and theorems stated outside the frozen appendix be boundary result nodes?
options: Include boundary nodes, because the appendix proves and sometimes reuses these body results.
Exclude target nodes, because the full statements are not in the frozen files.
ambiguities.recommended_resolution: Include boundary nodes with descriptions limited to what the appendix proof context establishes.
